_comment: Tier-2: CableNetApplication's own Register() exposes 5 elements with a Sliding/Ring/EmpiricalSpring vocabulary, NOT the simpler CableElement3D2N / MembraneElement3D3N / MembraneElement3D4N the catalog historically grouped under cable_net — those live in StructuralMechanicsApplication and are reachable only because CableNet's loader imports SMA first. Pitfall (kratos.cable_net #3). Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv on external ext4 image). MEASURED IN TWO SUBPROCESSES, because once both applications are loaded in one interpreter the split is invisible: with only StructuralMechanicsApplication imported, CableElement3D2N and both Membrane elements construct while SlidingCableElement3D3N, RingElement3D3N and EmpiricalSpringElement3D2N all raise 'is not registered'; with CableNetApplication imported, all six construct. That asymmetry is exactly the claim's point about what happens if a user loads CableNet in isolation or drops the SMA dependency. The fixture imports KratosMultiphysics at module scope; with Kratos absent the import raises, the process exits non-zero and the runner records a failure, never a pass. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 runs the "StructuralMechanics alone" probe with CableNetApplication imported as well, removing the isolation the registry-split claim rests on; the Sliding/Ring/EmpiricalSpring names then register in the supposedly SMA-only probe. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS and these expect_in_output strings disappear: sma_only[SlidingCableElement3D3N]=False, sma_only[RingElement3D3N]=False, sma_only[EmpiricalSpringElement3D2N]=False, cablenet_registry_split_mismatches=0. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/cablenet_registry_split_vs_structural && /usr/bin/python3 source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 /usr/bin/python3 source.py (fails). Interpreter: KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 is REQUIRED on this host -- the repo venv Kratos wheel is built against GLIBC_2.32 and fails to load (ImportError on Kratos.cpython-312...so), while the system python3.8 carries Kratos 10.4 Release with CableNet, ConstitutiveLaws, StructuralMechanics and LinearSolvers.
